A single integrable dominator for the difference quotients is constructed from the stated growth bounds, dominated convergence identifies the directional derivative, and boundedness in v follows. The growth hypotheses now allow an exceptional term: |f| <= C(1+|s|^p+|xi|^p) + G(x) with G in L^1 and |f_s|+|f_xi| <= C(1+|s|^{p-1}+|xi|^{p-1}) + g(x) with g in L^{p'}; the dominator acquires the term g(x)(|v|+|Dv|), integrable by Holder since g in L^{p'} and v,Dv in L^p. This relaxation is exactly what lets the L^2-forcing Dirichlet functional satisfy the lemma, and it weakens no previous case. Sources [T] Example 13.3 and [MA] Chapter 5 Proposition 5.1. Dependencies are the Gateaux definition, Caratheodory measurability and the published Sobolev and convergence items.
